failed_attempts.failure_scope: For the scalar pair U_s=b*y^4/4+gamma*y^2/2 and U_u=b*y^4/4-gamma*y^2/2, b,gamma>0, under any common label-independent admissible bounded feedback |g_t|<=G, |f_t|<=F, the internal proof and same-team audit give s*=[C+sqrt(C^2+4*b*H)]/(2*b), C=G+gamma+eta/2, H=1/beta+F^2/(2*eta), and KL(P_u[0,T]||P_s[0,T])<=mu*beta*gamma^2*T*s*. Thus fixed per-hypothesis error delta requires T >= (1-2*delta)*log((1-delta)/delta)/(mu*beta*gamma^2*s*)=Omega(sqrt(b)) at fixed positive mu,beta,gamma and fixed finite controls/eta. The result is conditional on the exact-reset, equal-noise, common bounded-control, full-path interface; it does not cover unbounded actuation, a hard clamp with force readout, changed temperature/mobility, direct force-law sensing, or arbitrary expected stopping time. External proof review and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

latest_substantive_result.summary: The principal mathematical result is a conditional information lower bound for a fully observed scalar thermal process with opposite-curvature quartic potentials U_s(y)=b*y^4/4+gamma*y^2/2 and U_u(y)=b*y^4/4-gamma*y^2/2. With b,gamma,mu,beta>0; exact reset Y(0)=0; the same known mobility and temperature; perfect continuous trajectory observation; and any common admissible causal randomized feedback with bounded gain |g_t|<=G and force |f_t|<=F, the audited moment bound is s*=[C+sqrt(C^2+4*b*H)]/(2*b), C=G+gamma+eta/2, H=1/beta+F^2/(2*eta), for any fixed eta>0. The path laws satisfy KL(P_u[0,T]||P_s[0,T])<=mu*beta*gamma^2*T*s*. A test with error <=delta<1/2 under each model therefore requires T >= (1-2*delta)*log((1-delta)/delta)/(mu*beta*gamma^2*s*)=Omega(sqrt(b)) at fixed mu,beta,gamma,G,F,eta; the same bound covers finitely many exact-reset trials with deterministic total interrogation cap. An independent same-team audit found no counterexample in this contract and supplied an exponential-Lyapunov Novikov proof. This refutes a uniformly fast native instability-screen inference from local negative curvature alone within the admitted class; it is not external proof review, priority clearance, or a physical device result. The strongest remaining physical construction is a proposed temporarily routed attached loop: one removable root partition forces a two-port wash around the loop, then local erasure restores the final attached-loop geometry. The next experiment is a root-seal/material-compatibility coupon followed by matched wash, vacuum/pressure, reversible-routing, and direct/assembled comparators with spatial residue and function assays. No experiment or new capability is established.
